Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

251	            ``(http_status, body)`` for the idempotent guard.
252	            """
253	            op_id = operation.operation_id
254	            body = {"error": message, "operation_id": op_id}
255	            # The accurate key_id rule: a restore's and a batch rotation's
256	            # events are always key_id null; rotate/import carry the (already
257	            # validated) key_id.
258	            kind = (operation.details or {}).get("kind")
259	            audit_key_id = (
260	                None if kind in ("restore", "batch_rotate")
261	                else (key_id if is_valid_key_id(key_id) else None)
262	            )
263	            audit_desc = {
264	                "action": action,
265	                "outcome": audit_mod.OUTCOME_REJECTED,
266	                "tenant_id": tenant_id,
267	                "key_id": audit_key_id,
268	            }
269	            operation_store.stage_terminal(
270	                operation, http_status, body, audit=audit_desc
271	            )
272	            store.audit_attempt(
273	                tenant_id, audit_key_id, action, audit_mod.OUTCOME_REJECTED,
274	                event_id=op_id,
275	            )
276	            return http_status, body

278	        def _idempotent_provider_terminal(
279	            self, operation, http_status, message
280	        ):
281	            """Persist a bound op's provider-failure terminal and append it.
282	
283	            A KMS/HSM load/contract/call/handle-delete failure (503) or a
284	            refusal of imported material (400) that happens *after* the
285	            Idempotency-Key is bound is a durable terminal state, exactly like
286	            a 403/404/409 refusal: the safe response is staged first, then a
287	            single ``rejected`` event named after the operation_id is appended
288	            (rotate projects the request key_id, import the in-bundle key_id,
289	            restore null), so HTTP/CLI retries and GET operation replay the
290	            same status/body byte-for-byte and the event is never duplicated.
291	            The body never carries the backend detail, a handle, material or
292	            a passphrase. A failure of the stage write or the ledger append
293	            propagates (the guard finalizes failed(500)); nothing committed.
294	            """
295	            op_id = operation.operation_id
296	            body = {"error": message, "operation_id": op_id}
297	            details = operation.details or {}
298	            kind = details.get("kind")
299	            if kind == "batch_rotate":
300	                action = audit_mod.ACTION_BATCH_ROTATE
301	            elif kind == "rotate":
302	                action = audit_mod.ACTION_ROTATE
303	            elif kind == "encrypt":
304	                action = audit_mod.ACTION_ENCRYPT
305	            elif kind == "migrate":
306	                action = audit_mod.ACTION_MIGRATE
307	            else:
308	                action = audit_mod.ACTION_IMPORT
309	            audit_key_id = (
310	                None if kind in ("restore", "batch_rotate")
311	                else (
312	                    details.get("key_id")
313	                    if is_valid_key_id(details.get("key_id"))
314	                    else None
315	                )
316	            )
317	            operation_store.stage_terminal(
318	                operation,
319	                http_status,
320	                body,
321	                audit={
322	                    "action": action,
323	                    "outcome": audit_mod.OUTCOME_REJECTED,
324	                    "tenant_id": operation.tenant_id,
325	                    "key_id": audit_key_id,
326	                },
327	            )
328	            store.audit_attempt(
329	                operation.tenant_id, audit_key_id, action,
330	                audit_mod.OUTCOME_REJECTED, event_id=op_id,
331	            )
332	            operation_store.finish(
333	                operation, operations_mod.STATUS_FAILED, http_status, body
334	            )
335	            self._send_json(http_status, body)

337	        def _timed_out_body(self, operation_id: str) -> dict:
338	            return {
339	                "error": "operation timed out waiting for a lock",
340	                "operation_id": operation_id,
341	            }

343	        def _strand_unavailable_body(self, operation_id: str) -> dict:
344	            # Material-safe: no handle, material, passphrase or path detail.
345	            return {
346	                "error": "temporary storage failure, please retry",
347	                "operation_id": operation_id,
348	            }

350	        def _send_strand_unavailable(self, operation_id, status: int) -> None:
351	            # The operation stays PENDING (no provider/key/handle/audit was
352	            # touched); the client retries with the same Idempotency-Key and
353	            # reuses this operation_id.

356	        def _idempotent_guard(self, path, tenant_id, operator, payload, key,
357	                              executor) -> None:
358	            """Bind the Idempotency-Key and run an idempotent mutation.
359	
360	            ``key`` is the already-validated Idempotency-Key. ``executor`` is
361	            ``executor(operation, mirror) -> (http_status, response_body)``
362	            and performs the mutation once; it may raise
363	            ProviderUnavailable / ProviderInvalidMaterial / LedgerError /
364	            LockTimeout. On a new binding the operation is persisted pending,
365	            its 0600/fsynced artifact mirror is created BEFORE any provider
366	            call, the mutation is executed once and the operation is recorded
367	            with its terminal status/response; an identical retry replays the
368	            stored result (no new audit event); a same-key/different-binding
369	            request gets 409 naming the original operation; waiting on an
370	            in-flight owner beyond 5 s answers timed_out (503) without
371	            writing anything.
372	
373	            If the 0600 mirror cannot be created (an OSError making the
374	            directory, temp file or rename) AFTER the key bound but BEFORE the
375	            first provider call, the bound operation is left pending and the
376	            request answers a material-safe 500/503: no provider, key, handle
377	            or audit is written, and a later identical HTTP/CLI request
378	            rebuilds the mirror and runs the attempt under the SAME
379	            operation_id.
380	            """
381	            normalized = operations_mod.normalize_body(payload)
382	            begin = operation_store.begin(
383	                tenant_id, operator, path, normalized, key
384	            )
385	            if begin.kind == "conflict":
386	                self._serve_conflict(begin.record)
387	                return
388	            if begin.kind == "replay":
389	                self._serve_replay_or_takeover(begin.record, executor)
390	                return
391	            self._run_owned_attempt(
392	                begin.record, executor, blocking=True, takeover=False
393	            )
394	
395	        def _serve_replay_or_takeover(self, record, executor) -> None:
396	            """Resolve an identical binding: replay a terminal, wait for a live
397	            owner, or take a dead owner's clean pre-provider strand over."""
398	            if record.is_terminal():
399	                self._replay_terminal(record)
400	                return
401	            if artifact_store is None:
402	                self._serve_pending_wait(record)
403	                return
404	            # Still pending. First try to claim the attempt immediately: if a
405	            # live owner (thread or process) holds it, fall back to the 5 s
406	            # wait. A dead owner with a clean, never-committed strand hands it
407	            # over under the same operation_id.
408	            try:
409	                self._run_owned_attempt(
410	                    record, executor, blocking=False, takeover=True
411	                )
412	            except BlockingIOError:
413	                self._serve_pending_wait(record)
414	
415	        def _run_owned_attempt(self, operation, executor, blocking,
416	                              takeover) -> None:
417	            """Run the attempt once, owning its mirror + claim for the window.
418	
419	            Used both by the binding winner (``takeover=False``) and by a
420	            retried identical request taking a stranded pending attempt over
421	            (``takeover=True``).
422	            """
423	            op_id = operation.operation_id
424	            if artifact_store is None:
425	                # Mirrors disabled (tests/legacy wiring): run directly.
426	                self._idempotent_run_body(operation, op_id, executor, None)
427	                return
428	            attempt_cm = artifact_store.attempt(
429	                operation, blocking, takeover=takeover,
430	                operation_store=operation_store if takeover else None,
431	            )
432	            try:
433	                mirror = attempt_cm.__enter__()
434	            except ArtifactAlreadyTerminal as already:
435	                # The owner reached a terminal while the claim was taken:
436	                # replay its fresh stored result verbatim, execute nothing.
437	                self._replay_terminal(already.record)
438	                return
439	            except ArtifactStrandUnavailable as exc:
440	                # Mirror claim/creation failed with the op still bound and
441	                # pending: surface 500/503 without finalizing it.
442	                self._send_strand_unavailable(op_id, exc.http_status)
443	                return
444	            except BlockingIOError:
445	                # A live owner holds the attempt; the caller waits.
446	                raise
447	            try:
448	                self._idempotent_run_body(
449	                    operation, op_id, executor, mirror
450	                )
451	            finally:
452	                # Committed: verified ownership then dropped; uncommitted:
453	                # dropped only once every rollback artifact is gone. A
454	                # mirror that cannot be verified survives for startup.
455	                try:
456	                    artifact_store.after_terminal(mirror)
457	                finally:
458	                    attempt_cm.__exit__(None, None, None)
459	
460	        def _idempotent_run_body(self, operation, op_id, executor, mirror):
461	            try:
462	                http_status, body = executor(operation, mirror)
463	            except ArtifactStrandUnavailable as exc:
464	                # The mirror could not be described/tied in before the first
465	                # provider call, or a clean strand could not be taken over.
466	                # Nothing committed: leave the operation PENDING and answer
467	                # 500/503. A same-key HTTP/CLI retry reuses the operation_id.
468	                self._send_strand_unavailable(op_id, exc.http_status)
469	                return
470	            except LockTimeout:
471	                # Lock wait exceeded 5 s: no key, audit event or handle was
472	                # written. Record and answer timed_out (503).
473	                body = self._timed_out_body(op_id)
474	                operation_store.finish(
475	                    operation, operations_mod.STATUS_TIMED_OUT, 503, body
476	                )
477	                self._send_json(503, body)
478	                return
479	            except ProviderInvalidMaterial as exc:
480	                # A bound refusal of imported material is a terminal 400:
481	                # stage the field-naming error, append its single rejected
482	                # event and finish. A failure of that persistence itself
483	                # becomes failed(500) below; nothing committed.
484	                try:
485	                    self._idempotent_provider_terminal(
486	                        operation, 400, str(exc)
487	                    )
488	                    return
489	                except (OSError, LedgerError) as persist_exc:
490	                    body = {
491	                        "error": _ledger_failure_text(persist_exc),
492	                        "operation_id": op_id,
493	                    }
494	                    operation_store.finish(
495	                        operation, operations_mod.STATUS_FAILED, 500, body
496	                    )
497	                    self._send_json(500, body)
498	                    return
499	            except MigrationTransferParked:
500	                # A direct ciphertext-transfer migrate failed before its
501	                # commit point and its new-handle cleanup could not be fully
502	                # confirmed: the migration snapshot, provision journal and
503	                # mirror are deliberately RETAINED for startup. The operation
504	                # stays PENDING with NO audit event; only the fixed safe 503
505	                # is sent (never resetting the mirror, which is the restart's
506	                # rollback index).
507	                body = {
508	                    "error": "key management provider is unavailable",
509	                    "operation_id": op_id,
510	                }
511	                self._send_json(503, body)
512	                return
513	            except ProviderReconnectPending:
514	                # The provider call never effectively started: either it
515	                # waited out the shared five-second reconnect gate, or the
516	                # provider now active carries a different provider_id than the
517	                # one this pending operation is bound to. No audit event was
518	                # appended and nothing committed; the store's abort path
519	                # already removed any (empty) journal and minted no handle.
520	                # Reset the mirror to a clean bound strand, leave the
521	                # operation PENDING and answer the fixed safe 503, so a retry
522	                # once reconnect settles -- or a provider with the same id
523	                # reconnects -- continues under the SAME operation_id/
524	                # event_id, which is therefore never duplicated.
525	                if mirror is not None:
526	                    try:
527	                        mirror.reset_for_pending_retry()
528	                    except OSError:
529	                        # A reset that cannot persist leaves after_terminal to
530	                        # decide from the durable facts (it retains or parks
531	                        # anything with surviving evidence).
532	                        pass
533	                body = {
534	                    "error": "key management provider is unavailable",
535	                    "operation_id": op_id,
536	                }
537	                self._send_json(503, body)
538	                return
539	            except ProviderUnavailable:
540	                # A bound KMS/HSM fault (load/contract/call/handle-delete) is
541	                # a durable terminal 503 with the fixed safe message and one
542	                # rejected event named after the operation_id; retries replay
543	                # it verbatim. Persistence failure becomes failed(500).
544	                try:
545	                    self._idempotent_provider_terminal(
546	                        operation, 503,
547	                        "key management provider is unavailable",
548	                    )
549	                    return
550	                except (OSError, LedgerError) as persist_exc:
551	                    body = {
552	                        "error": _ledger_failure_text(persist_exc),
553	                        "operation_id": op_id,
554	                    }
555	                    operation_store.finish(
556	                        operation, operations_mod.STATUS_FAILED, 500, body
557	                    )
558	                    self._send_json(500, body)
559	                    return
560	            except OSError as exc:
561	                # Persisting the staged result (or another pre-commit write)
562	                # failed before the commit-point append: the store already
563	                # rolled back the file and minted handles, so nothing
564	                # committed. Finalize failed(500).
565	                body = {
566	                    "error": "audit ledger failure: %s" % exc,
567	                    "operation_id": op_id,
568	                }
569	                operation_store.finish(
570	                    operation, operations_mod.STATUS_FAILED, 500, body
571	                )
572	                self._send_json(500, body)
573	                return
574	            except LedgerError:
575	                body = {
576	                    "error": LEDGER_UNAVAILABLE,
577	                    "operation_id": op_id,
578	                }
579	                operation_store.finish(
580	                    operation, operations_mod.STATUS_FAILED, 500, body
581	                )
582	                self._send_json(500, body)
583	                return
584	            body = dict(body)
585	            body["operation_id"] = op_id
586	            state = self._op_state_for_status(http_status)
587	            operation_store.finish(operation, state, http_status, body)
588	            self._send_json(http_status, body)

612	        def _operator(self):
613	            """Return the single non-empty X-Operator-Id, else send 400.
614	
615	            Duplicate headers are a 400 as well. A missing/empty operator is
616	            rejected before any tenant-scoped work happens.
617	            """
618	            values = self.headers.get_all("X-Operator-Id") or []
619	            if len(values) > 1:
620	                self._bad_request(
621	                    "duplicate X-Operator-Id (provide a single header)"
622	                )
623	                return None
624	            operator = values[0] if values else None
625	            if not operator:
626	                self._bad_request(
627	                    "missing required header: X-Operator-Id"
628	                    if operator is None
629	                    else "header X-Operator-Id must be a non-empty string"
630	                )

634	        def _enforce(self, tenant_id, key_id, action, operator) -> bool:
635	            """Enforce the tenant policy. True to proceed; else response sent.
636	
637	            A rejection is a 403 carrying a rejected audit event that records
638	            the original action and key_id; unknown/cross-tenant keys remain
639	            404 and are handled by callers after enforcement.
640	            """
641	            try:
642	                allowed = policy_store.is_allowed(
643	                    tenant_id, action, operator
644	                )
645	            except PolicyStoreUnavailable:
646	                # Backend corruption must never fail open: fixed 500 with no
647	                # success or rejection audit event.
648	                self._send_json(
649	                    500, {"error": "policy store is unavailable"}
650	                )
651	                return False
652	            if allowed:
653	                return True

661	        # -- parsing helpers ---------------------------------------------
662	        def _read_json_object(self, audit: bool = True,
663	                              parse_conflict=None):
664	            """Return the request body as a dict, or None after responding.
665	
666	            A body that cannot be parsed carries no usable tenant. By default
667	            an invisible tenant_conflict is written before the 400 (and a
668	            ledger failure turns the answer into 500). The idempotent
669	            mutation endpoints pass ``audit=False``: an Idempotency-Key has
670	            already been validated on them, but no operation is bound yet, so
671	            a parse/parameter failure must leave no audit event, operation
672	            record, key or provider handle behind. A non-idempotent endpoint
673	            can pass ``parse_conflict=False`` while leaving ``audit=True``:
674	            the parse/non-object 400 is a plain body error that writes
675	            nothing, while a later tenant-parameter failure on the SAME body
676	            still records its invisible tenant_conflict (sign/verify).
677	            """
678	            write_conflict = (
679	                audit if parse_conflict is None else parse_conflict
680	            )
681	
682	            def bad(message: str) -> None:
683	                if not write_conflict or self._record_conflict():
684	                    self._bad_request(message)
685	
686	            try:
687	                length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", 0))
688	            except ValueError:
689	                bad("invalid Content-Length")
690	                return None
691	            raw = self.rfile.read(length) if length > 0 else b""
692	            try:
693	                payload = json.loads(raw.decode("utf-8"))
694	            except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):
695	                bad("request body must be valid JSON")
696	                return None
697	            if not isinstance(payload, dict):
698	                bad("request body must be a JSON object")
699	                return None
700	            return payload

702	        def _tenant(self, parts, body=_MISSING, audit: bool = True):
703	            """Resolve tenant from X-Tenant-Id / query / JSON body.
704	
705	            Returns the tenant id, or None after sending 400. A duplicated
706	            X-Tenant-Id header or a duplicated tenant_id query parameter is a
707	            400 naming tenant_id, as is any disagreement between the sources;
708	            several sources carrying the *same* value are accepted. Every
709	            failure is written to the ledger as an invisible tenant_conflict
710	            event, except on the idempotent endpoints before their key is
711	            bound (``audit=False``): such a parameter failure must leave no
712	            audit event behind.
713	            """
714	            def fail(message: str) -> None:
715	                if not audit or self._record_conflict():
716	                    self._bad_request(message)
717	
718	            headers = self.headers.get_all("X-Tenant-Id") or []
719	            if len(headers) > 1:
720	                fail("duplicate tenant_id (provide a single X-Tenant-Id header)")
721	                return None
722	            query_values = parse_qs(
723	                parts.query, keep_blank_values=True
724	            ).get("tenant_id", [])
725	            if len(query_values) > 1:
726	                fail("duplicate tenant_id (provide a single tenant_id parameter)")
727	                return None
728	
729	            candidates = []
730	            if headers:
731	                candidates.append(headers[0])
732	            if query_values:
733	                candidates.append(query_values[0])
734	            if body is not _MISSING:
735	                body_tenant = body.get("tenant_id")
736	                if body_tenant is not None:
737	                    if not isinstance(body_tenant, str) or not body_tenant:
738	                        fail("field tenant_id must be a non-empty string")
739	                        return None
740	                    candidates.append(body_tenant)
741	            distinct = set(candidates)
742	            if len(distinct) > 1:
743	                fail(
744	                    "conflicting tenant_id parameters (header, query and body must agree)"
745	                )
746	                return None
747	            if not distinct:
748	                fail("missing required field: tenant_id")
749	                return None
750	            tenant = next(iter(distinct))
751	            if not tenant:
752	                fail("field tenant_id must be a non-empty string")
753	                return None
754	            return tenant

756	        def _audit_tenant(self, parts):
757	            """Resolve the single-source tenant for GET /v1/audit.
758	
759	            Exactly one of a single X-Tenant-Id header or a single
760	            ?tenant_id= parameter must supply it. Any missing/duplicate/
761	            empty/conflicting value is a 400 naming tenant_id and is written
762	            to the ledger as an invisible tenant_conflict event, like every
763	            other tenant-parameter failure.
764	            """
765	            def fail(message: str) -> None:
766	                if self._record_conflict():
767	                    self._bad_request(message)
768	
769	            headers = self.headers.get_all("X-Tenant-Id") or []
770	            if len(headers) > 1:
771	                fail(
772	                    "duplicate tenant_id (provide a single X-Tenant-Id header)"
773	                )
774	                return None
775	            query_values = parse_qs(parts.query, keep_blank_values=True).get(
776	                "tenant_id", []
777	            )
778	            if len(query_values) > 1:
779	                fail(

786	                )

790	            )

793	                return None
794	            if not tenant:

796	                return None
